tasks.commitBody:
The agenda's narrative date headers and the event-detail date line
followed the device locale — an Estonian user with an English
phone read 'TUESDAY, MARCH 23' in an app that is otherwise
entirely Estonian (visible in Joosep's 2026-09-05 screenshot,
reported by nobody, which is part of why it mattered).

Both formatters now take the app language from Paraglide's
getLocale(), and they are constructed reactively: a locale change
rebuilds them without relying on setLocale's current full-page
reload, so removing that reload later cannot silently regress the
headers. Only the locale argument changed — the DST-guarded
options, the noon-anchored day construction and the TZ constant
are byte-identical, and the ISO producers (groupKeyFmt,
shortDateFmt) keep their deliberate 'en-CA' per the #207/#212
rulings, pinned by a test that grouping keys stay ISO under every
app language.

Per done-when 5, stated rather than guessed: #250 kept the CSS
uppercase treatment, so Estonian's mid-sentence lowercase
convention does not show today — but the text beneath the CSS is
now the natural-case Estonian Intl output, so if the uppercase
treatment ever goes, the words are already right.

Live gate (Joosep): set the app to Estonian on an English-locale
phone — the agenda headers read 'teisipäev, 23. märts' (shown
uppercased), not 'TUESDAY, MARCH 23'; same on the event page.
Switch to lv/uk — headers follow.
